Tapping the button is not enough: at the tap (12:06:15) the driver was 600 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 0 s afterwards (F5), and the platform never recorded him at the pickup (F4), so NS-1 (i)-(ii) are not satisfied.

The rider's 12:07 message "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" is consistent with the GPS record that the car was 600 m away (F9, F1); the driver's own 12:06 message claiming "I'm here already" (F8) is the statement the system record contradicts, so no rider no-show can be built on it.

The amount is not in dispute - $6.61 is the single published fee (F6) - but a fee that is correctly quantified is still chargeable only if NS-1's conditions are met, and they are not (F5, F4); NS-1 is the gateway via NS-0.

Profile facts cannot decide the case (they may only support an added action), and the driver's prior upheld no-show dispute (F17) makes this repeated rather than an isolated lapse, supporting our flag_account request.

We agree the chat record is complete and timestamped (F11), which is exactly why the contradiction is resolvable against the driver: the chat says he was at the pickup (F8) while GPS and the timeline say he never was (F1, F4, F5).

Our refund claim stands and is reinforced by the opponent's own concessions: the driver tapped "I'm Here" 600 m away and never came within 200 m (F5, F1), so under NS-2 the $6.61 must be refunded in full and the abuse limb adds flag_account.

The duration limb nonetheless holds — 3 min 30 s of continuous waiting until cancellation (F2, F3) — and the sanctioned consequence of a mis-located tap under NS-2 is the account referral, not a windfall refund for a rider who also never appeared (F9).

F9 is a rider statement of position, not a system record, and the system records place the driver 600 m away (F1) while placing the rider nowhere at all; under the system-records-first rule F9 cannot establish the rider's presence, and it equally shows he was on the app and knew the car had not been found (F9, F8).
Conceded: F12 (driver statement) is contradicted by F5, F1 and F2 and must give way; I withdraw any reliance on F12 and ask the judge to decide on the GPS and timeline facts alone.

This is the one rider point that bites, and I accept the NS-2 consequence on its own terms: F5 supports an account referral for the ill-placed arrival tap. A `flag_account` referral is an account-review action, not a monetary refund, so it cannot convert into the rider's $6.61 refund claim (F6, F17).

Profile facts may only support an additional action and never decide the case: F17 shows one upheld no-show dispute in 90 days for an account with 464 trips in 90 days and a 4.67 rating, which is a reliability record, not proof of repetition here.

Accepted that no traffic or weather excuse exists: F14 records no incidents near the route and F15 gives fair weather, 0.0 mm rain, so the driver has no RD-4 justification for stopping 600 m from the pickup (F13 is only a 20–29 km/h band).

The amount is not in issue — F6 is $6.61 and F7 shows 1.0x with no surge — but a refund under NS-2 requires NS-1 (i)-(iii) to fail in a way that leaves the rider blameless, and the record shows the driver waited 3 min 30 s until 12:09:25 (F2, F3) while the rider's only action was a message at 12:07 (F9, F11).

I withdraw nothing in D4 but narrow it: the fee on the record is the single published $6.61 cancellation amount (F6, F7), which is exactly why the outcome should be a fee review in my client's favour only if the judge finds the wait location irrelevant — the judge may instead order the fee waived and record the NS-2 referral (F5).

events.body:
This is a no-show (waiting/cancellation fee) dispute under RydeX, cancelled by the driver [F3], so it enters through NS-0 and is tested against NS-1. The $6.61 fee on the fare record is the single published cancellation fee and no surge applied [F6][F7], so the quantum is not in issue; the question is whether NS-1's conditions for charging it are met [NS-0][FARE-1].

NS-1 requires (i) an arrival indication, (ii) that at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the driver was at the pickup point, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting there until cancellation. The GPS record settles all three: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while 600 m from the pickup [F5], his closest approach over the whole window was 599 m at 12:06:55 [F1], he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap [F5], and he was stationary 600 m away from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 [F2]. The timeline confirms the platform never recorded him at the pickup at all (driver_arrived_at null) [F4]. So conditions (ii) and (iii) fail [NS-1].

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while GPS placed him 600 m from the pickup point, so NS-1 (ii) fails: he was not at the pick-up location according to GPS data when he declared arrival.

The record shows the driver was never at the pickup point at all: his closest approach was 599 m at 12:06:55 and he never came within 200 m, and driver_arrived_at is null because the platform never recorded him at the pickup point.

The rider was at the pickup point and said so at 12:07 while the driver's car was nowhere near: chat #2 reads "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?", contradicting the driver's claim that the rider never showed up.

The rider knew the driver was waiting and did not appear: the rider's 12:07 message says "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?", yet after that the driver waited a further ~2 minutes to 12:09:25 before cancelling as a no-show.

The rider never contested the charge at the time and the record shows the $6.61 cancellation fee with no surge and no other added item, so the fee is exactly the single published cancellation-fee amount.

Tapping the button is not enough: at the tap (12:06:15) the driver was 600 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 0 s afterwards (F5), and the platform never recorded him at the pickup (F4), so NS-1 (i)-(ii) are not satisfied.

The rider's 12:07 message "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" is consistent with the GPS record that the car was 600 m away (F9, F1); the driver's own 12:06 message claiming "I'm here already" (F8) is the statement the system record contradicts, so no rider no-show can be built on it.

The amount is not in dispute - $6.61 is the single published fee (F6) - but a fee that is correctly quantified is still chargeable only if NS-1's conditions are met, and they are not (F5, F4); NS-1 is the gateway via NS-0.

Profile facts cannot decide the case (they may only support an added action), and the driver's prior upheld no-show dispute (F17) makes this repeated rather than an isolated lapse, supporting our flag_account request.

We agree the chat record is complete and timestamped (F11), which is exactly why the contradiction is resolvable against the driver: the chat says he was at the pickup (F8) while GPS and the timeline say he never was (F1, F4, F5).

Our refund claim stands and is reinforced by the opponent's own concessions: the driver tapped "I'm Here" 600 m away and never came within 200 m (F5, F1), so under NS-2 the $6.61 must be refunded in full and the abuse limb adds flag_account.

Conceded on the record: F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 12:06:15 was made 600 m from the pickup point and F1 confirms the closest approach was 599 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails. I do not contest that limb; my case rests on the completed wait duration and the rider's non-appearance (F2, F3, F9).

Accepted as to the GPS record: F1 gives a closest approach of 599 m and F4 shows driver_arrived_at is null, so the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point. That is a location failure, not a fraud finding, and it does not by itself entitle the rider to a refund where the driver completed a genuine 3 min 30 s stationary wait (F2).

Part-conceded: the stationary period F2 ran 12:05:55–12:09:25 at 600 m from the pickup and F5 records 0 s within 200 m after the tap, so the wait was not at the pickup point. The duration limb nonetheless holds — 3 min 30 s of continuous waiting until cancellation (F2, F3) — and the sanctioned consequence of a mis-located tap under NS-2 is the account referral, not a windfall refund for a rider who also never appeared (F9).

Contested: I do not dispute that NS-1 (ii) fails, but the rider points to no fact showing he was at the pickup point, and his own 12:07 message (F9) is the only record of his position; where neither party's arrival is GPS-confirmed the record does not support a full refund, and my client's 3 min 30 s stationary wait (F2) is the only verified waiting conduct in the file.

F9 is a rider statement of position, not a system record, and the system records place the driver 600 m away (F1) while placing the rider nowhere at all; under the system-records-first rule F9 cannot establish the rider's presence, and it equally shows he was on the app and knew the car had not been found (F9, F8).
Conceded: F12 (driver statement) is contradicted by F5, F1 and F2 and must give way; I withdraw any reliance on F12 and ask the judge to decide on the GPS and timeline facts alone.

This is the one rider point that bites, and I accept the NS-2 consequence on its own terms: F5 supports an account referral for the ill-placed arrival tap. A `flag_account` referral is an account-review action, not a monetary refund, so it cannot convert into the rider's $6.61 refund claim (F6, F17).

Profile facts may only support an additional action and never decide the case: F17 shows one upheld no-show dispute in 90 days for an account with 464 trips in 90 days and a 4.67 rating, which is a reliability record, not proof of repetition here.

Accepted that no traffic or weather excuse exists: F14 records no incidents near the route and F15 gives fair weather, 0.0 mm rain, so the driver has no RD-4 justification for stopping 600 m from the pickup (F13 is only a 20–29 km/h band).

The amount is not in issue — F6 is $6.61 and F7 shows 1.0x with no surge — but a refund under NS-2 requires NS-1 (i)-(iii) to fail in a way that leaves the rider blameless, and the record shows the driver waited 3 min 30 s until 12:09:25 (F2, F3) while the rider's only action was a message at 12:07 (F9, F11).

I withdraw nothing in D4 but narrow it: the fee on the record is the single published $6.61 cancellation amount (F6, F7), which is exactly why the outcome should be a fee review in my client's favour only if the judge finds the wait location irrelevant — the judge may instead order the fee waived and record the NS-2 referral (F5).
